result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers correctly identify the roughly 1.65:1 text-on-background contrast, the flat button hierarchy and the mid-tone khaki background, and their quoted ratios check out. B ranks the problems explicitly by impact and gives a full, mostly verifiable replacement palette that keeps the warmth. It also gives a reasoned note on why it changed hue family. A gives only rough fix directions and ends by offering more work instead of giving the palette. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers correctly name unreadable body text (about 1.7:1) as the main problem and explain the muddiness in terms of these specific values. Their contrast figures hold up when checked against the WCAG formula. A wins because it gives a complete, warm replacement palette with contrast checks for each role, while B gives mostly direction and leaves the primary color undecided, though B does usefully point out that the primary button barely stands out from the page.
